title: Measuring microtubule binding kinetics of membrane-bound kinesin motors using supported lipid bilayers
protocol: Make solutions for the accumulation assay.
Prepare Motor buffer (2 mM ATP, 1 mM DTT, 20 mM D-glucose) by mixing 969 μL BRB80 with 20 μL MgATP (100 mM), 1 μL DTT (1 M), and 10 μL D-glucose (2 M).
Prepare Motility buffer (1 μM taxol, 2 mM ATP, 1 mM DTT, 40 mM D-glucose) by mixing 958 μL BRB80 with 1 μL taxol (1 mM), 20 μL MgATP (100 mM), 1 μL DTT (1 M), and 20 μL D-glucose (2 M).
Prepare Motor buffer (1 mM DTT, 20 mM D-glucose) by mixing 989 μL BRB80 with 1 μL DTT (1 M) and 10 μL D-glucose (2 M).
Prepare Motility buffer (1 μM taxol, 2 mM AMPPNP, 1 mM DTT, 40 mM D-glucose) by mixing 938 μL BRB80 with 1 μL taxol (1 mM), 40 μL MgAMPPNP (50 mM), 1 μL DTT (1 M), and 20 μL D-glucose (2 M).
Use a plasma cleaner to treat one of the annealed coverslips on high RF level for 5 minutes.
Allow SUVs to come to 20°C–24°C.
Cut a small piece of PDMS (∼1 cm × 1 cm, ∼1 mm thick) and use a 6 mm biopsy punch to cut a well in the center.
Remove dust from the PDMS spacer by a piece of tape.
Place the spacer on a plasma-treated coverslip.
Add 50 μL of SUVs to the well.
Incubate for 10 minutes.
Wash with 50 μL BRB80.
Mix solution by gently pipetting approximately 5 times.
Remove 50 μL of the solution from the well.
Repeat washing steps until a total of 500 μL BRB80 has been used.
Add 50 μL motor buffer to the well.
Mix solution by gently pipetting.
Remove 50 μL of the solution from the well.
Repeat washing with motor buffer until a total of 300 μL has been used.
Add 50 μL active kinesin-NeutrAvidin complexes at 20°C–24°C to the well.
Gently pipet a few times to mix.
Incubate for 10 minutes.
Wash with 50 μL motility buffer.
Repeat washing steps until a total of 250 μL motility buffer has been used.
Add 50 μL motility buffer to the sample well to make a total volume of 100 μL.
Add 1 μL glucose oxidase and 1 μL catalase to the well.
Gently mix the solution using a p100/p200 pipet set to 50 μL.
Check SLB quality by Atto 647N fluorescence.
Check motor signal homogeneity by GFP fluorescence using TIRF microscope.
Move the sample to a new region.
Add microtubules made in step 20a under the ‘Before you begin’ section (final concentration 16–32 nM).
Pipette quickly and gently to mix.
Immediately start taking a video in the GFP channel.
Once a video is finished, quickly find another region of interest.
Start taking the next video.
Take 3 videos per sample.
Choose frame rate and movie duration according to binding kinetics.
For kinesin-1 motors, take 100-s videos at 10 fps.
At high motor densities, add a saturating amount of kinesin-NeutrAvidin complexes to the SLB.
Control motor density by varying the fraction of DSPE-PEG(2000) Biotin (0.1%–0.6%) in the SLB.
Incubate SLBs containing 0.1% DSPE-PEG(2000) Biotin with kinesin-free NeutrAvidin spiked with varying amounts of kinesin-NeutrAvidin complexes.
Maintain a total concentration of kinesin-free NeutrAvidin and kinesin-NeutrAvidin at 50 nM for low motor densities.
Add at least 5 nM kinesin-NeutrAvidin to observe motor accumulation for kinesin-1 motors.
Take snapshots of the GFP signal in 5 different regions for each sample.
Calculate the mean intensity of the GFP signal.
Plot GFP intensity against the equivalent biotin concentration in the SLB (DSPE-PEG(2000) Biotin (%) × [kinesin-NeutrAvidin]/50 nM).
Proceed with motor counting if there is a linear relationship between GFP intensity and biotin concentration.

Use spiking ratios of kinesin-NeutrAvidin (0.3–1 nM) to free NeutrAvidin on SLBs containing 0.1% DSPE-PEG(2000) Biotin for motor counting under conditions where individual molecules can be visualized.
